Subject: Unusual auth failures on Feb 8 — request for IR timeline & redacted logs

Hi Kimberly,

On Feb 8 (UTC) we observed a 12-minute window of elevated auth failures hitting our Redwood integration (see internal ops ticket attached). No customer data appears missing from our side but our compliance team is requesting a formal incident timeline, root-cause summary, and redacted logs we can store with our records for SOC 2. Specifically we need: 

- A concise incident timeline (events, durations, mitigations)
- Auth-related logs (token issuance, refresh events, error codes) with user identifiers pseudonymized
- Confirmation whether any tokens or payloads were exfiltrated

Our legal team also asked for a signed statement that the data you provide has been redacted to remove PII and user emails. Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? We need the package by Feb 17 to align with our auditor.

Thanks in advance — this is routine but time-sensitive.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Ops, MedicoSys

Kimberly / Soojin — quick forensic plan and notes for the package INF-2781: 

What we'll include:
- forensics_timeline_20270208-02.txt — minute-by-minute events (relay handoffs, cache misses, error bursts)
- medicosys_sanitized_logs_20270208.csv — auth events, status codes, response latencies; user identifiers hashed with HMAC (per legal request)
- a short root-cause summary (config drift in token-cache eviction policy)

Redaction approach:
- Email addresses: replaced with vendor_hash(e-mail) values; original emails removed
- IP addresses: replaced with country/region only (no precise IPs)
- Session tokens, refresh tokens: not included; we will include token issuance events but not token values

Open questions for Marissa (privacy review): is HMAC with key rotation acceptable to MedicoSys legal, or do they require irreversible pseudonymization? Also need confirmation from Kimberly for file delivery method (SFTP, secure HubSpot upload).

I will assemble artifacts and initial timeline by EOD Feb 15 for internal review; final package to external by Feb 16 as requested.

- For delivery, our preference is SFTP (credentials below) or a secure HubSpot file link. I'll ask legal to confirm whether the signed cover letter can be a PDF scan.
- Critical: please confirm explicitly that there is no evidence of data exfiltration — we need that language for our auditor.

Upload details: sftp://files.medicosys.com/incoming/Redwood_IRP_20270216 (drop zone). Credentials will be provided to your GCP service account; I can share with Diego directly.

Alex / Legal team — please find the incident package for Feb 8 attached and delivered to your SFTP drop zone. Summary highlights below; full artifacts are attached as stubs and available at the hubspot record listed.

Executive summary:
- Window: 2027-02-08 14:03:12 UTC — 2027-02-08 14:15:08 UTC (12m)
- Root cause: token-cache eviction misconfiguration causing elevated token-miss rates and cascade retries; mitigated by rolling kernel cache adjustment at 14:18 UTC
- Impact: increased auth failures for a subset of sessions; no evidence of data exfiltration or token leakage in our analysis

Deliverables (attached / uploaded):
- redwood_irp_summary_20270216.pdf (signed cover statement; includes scope, mitigations, and remediation timeline)
- forensics_timeline_20270208-02.txt (minute-level events, anonymized)
- medicosys_sanitized_logs_20270208.csv (auth events, irreversible salted hashes for user identifiers, geolocation for IPs)

Notes on redaction and legal compliance:
- We used one-way salted SHA-256 with a per-report salt (irreversible) for user identifiers to meet your auditor requirement. Salt metadata not included in the delivered bundle.
- No full tokens, refresh tokens, or raw PII are present in the delivered CSV.

Action items and next steps:
- If MedicoSys legal requires an execution page for the cover letter, we can provide a signed PDF (attached) or execute a DocuSign — please advise.
- We recommend a short review call to walk through artifacts and answer auditor questions. Propose Wed Feb 18 (10:00–10:30 PT) — happy to set.
